In contrast, inductive reasoning is a type of reasoning in which a conclusion is drawn from a set of data or observations. In this method, the relationship between premises and conclusion is probable.

[Original Text]

Inductive reasoning, on the other hand, involves starting with specific observations or instances and deriving a general conclusion or hypothesis based on those observations. Deductive reasoning relies on logical deduction and formal inference, while inductive reasoning relies on pattern recognition and probabilistic inference. Deductive reasoning is more certain and reliable, while inductive reasoning is more uncertain and subject to revision as new evidence or information becomes available.
